title: Actual tower adjoint compositors and their reductions
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y,Z$, and smooth $k$-morphisms $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For a finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring $R$, use ordinary uncompleted constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,R}=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for bounded intrinsically constructible finite-Tor complexes [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], and $F_{h,R}=Rh_{!,R}\dashv H_{h,R}=h_R^!$ with counit $\varepsilon_{h,R}$ for $h=f,g,gf$ [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. Compactifications are coefficient independent.

Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$. A strict varying-coefficient tower consists of $A_n$-module sheaves $C_n$ with semilinear transitions $C_{n+1}\to C_n$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Work in its ordinary derived category and its full subcategory $\mathcal T_T$ where finite-level cohomological and Tor intervals can be chosen independently of $n$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. A tower is normalized when each derived reduction $r^C_{n,m}:C_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\to C_m$, $1\leq m\leq n$, is invertible. Use the actual tower functors $F_{h,\bullet}=Rh_{!,\bullet}$ and $H_{h,\bullet}=h_\bullet^!$ and their adjunctions of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels, det-sp-tower-gluing]; their finite evaluations preserve units and counits. Let $b_h,c_h$ be the finite coefficient comparisons of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image, det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. Use the finite proper/open compositors $\alpha_{A_n}$ [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons, lem-sp-finite-compact-site-coherence] and their counit-normalized right-adjoint comparisons $\theta_{A_n}$ [lem-sp-finite-adjoint-compositor-transposes]. Assume their finite $b$ and $c$ composition identities, with the compositors inserted as in that node.

On $\mathcal T$ there are natural isomorphisms of actual derived-tower functors
$$\alpha_\bullet:F_{g,\bullet}F_{f,\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gf,\bullet},\qquad
\theta_\bullet:H_{gf,\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{f,\bullet}H_{g,\bullet}.$$
The left comparison is the proper/open tower compositor; the right comparison is the unique adjunction comparison through it, with composite counit $\varepsilon_{g,\bullet}\circ F_{g,\bullet}(\varepsilon_{f,\bullet}H_{g,\bullet})$. Their evaluations are $\alpha_{A_n}$ and $\theta_{A_n}$ under the specified finite evaluation identifications, including counits. All six functors preserve the stated uniform constructible finite-Tor subcategories and their normalized full subcategories. More precisely their reduction maps are
$$r^{F_hC}_{n,m}=F_{h,A_m}(r^C_{n,m})\circ b_h(C_n),\qquad
r^{H_hC}_{n,m}=H_{h,A_m}(r^C_{n,m})\circ c_h(C_n).$$
Both evaluated compositors commute with these derived reduction maps for every $m\leq n$. The comparison isomorphisms exist in the tower derived categories before evaluation; no faithfulness of evaluation on derived morphisms is assumed.

proof.text: The hypotheses already supply the actual proper/open tower composition iso in cal.composition.composition and uniform ctf preservation in each Pair.closed. Lift this iso componentwise through the full ctf subcategory. It is the required alpha and its proper_open equation is reflexivity. The finite-evaluation lemma gives its left_evaluation equation.

Compose Pf.adj and Pg.adj. Transport Ph.adj along alpha inverse and use rightAdjointUniq to obtain theta. Its counit equation is Mathlib rightAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit. Equality of the inverse composite Hom transposes proves uniqueness, and comp_counit_app gives the composite counit.

Package each specified finite evaluation as an AdjunctionEvaluation using Pair.levels.unit and .counit. The private evaluation_transpose calculation expands the Hom bijection and uses these equations and naturality. Apply it successively for f and g to the transpose defining theta. The left_evaluation equation rewrites the resulting inverse left-comparison word into alpha_n followed by the inverse h evaluation. The counit equation of finiteTheta and the h counit-evaluation equation give the same finite inverse transpose on the other side. Injectivity of the finite composite Hom equivalence proves right_evaluation.

All Evaluation.comparison values for a fixed compactification and level are equal, because their normalization fields give the identical explicit word. Replace each supplied support evaluation with cal.finite.evaluation in cal.reduction.reduction_formula to obtain the left reduction formula. The right formula is Pair.levels.reduction verbatim. Apply this to f,g,fg.

For a normalized input, its intrinsic reduction is invertible because it is the recorded normalized reduction preceded by the inverse scalar-coordinate iso. The left coefficient comparison is invertible by cal.reduction.reduction_comparison_isIso. The right one is invertible by Pair.levels.coefficient_iso. In each reduction equation, functors preserve these isomorphisms; cancel the evaluation iso to see that the image intrinsic reduction is invertible, then cancel the scalar-coordinate iso. This proves preservation of normalized towers by all six already uniform ctf functors.

The reduction square for any actual tower morphism is cal.reduction.reduction_naturality. Apply it to each component of alpha and theta. This proves both squares for all m<=n, without evaluating equality of arbitrary derived tower morphisms and without needing the assumed finite b/c identities.

theorem towerAdjointCompositorRealization
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (_hpl : p ≠ l) (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Z.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (Z ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Z ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Z ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] [g.IsOver (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (d e : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension e g]
    (z : SpTowerCalculus.FiniteCoordinates l E)
    (hP : SpTowerCalculus.Preservation l E k b o q)
    (cal : SpTowerCalculus.Calculus l E k b o q z hP)
    (Pf : Pair l E b o q cf) (Pg : Pair l E b o q cg) (Ph : Pair l E b o q ch)
    (A : ∀ n : ℕ, FiniteAdjointCompositorDatum (SpTowerShriek.R l E n) cf cg ch)
    (_finiteIdentities : FiniteIdentities l E b o q Pf Pg Ph A) :
    ∃ alpha : left l E b o q Pf ⋙ left l E b o q Pg ≅ left l E b o q Ph,
    ∃ theta : Ph.right ≅ Pg.right ⋙ Pf.right,
      Laws l E b o q k z hP cal Pf Pg Ph A alpha theta
